calls.notes:
I built `designed.tsx`: a coral-reef seabed with an octopus that turns from coral orange to rock brown, raises skin horns, and shows its chromatophore pigment cells close up. Nothing was rendered, so the framing, timing and how far the colour shells overlap still need a visual check.
Recognition feature 1 is the eight arms with pale suckers, curled tips and webbing between them, built from Tube arms with Ball suckers and a low Cone web.
Recognition feature 2 is the bulbous mantle tilted back behind the head, built as a Lathe sac on a pivot set at -0.5 rad behind the Ball head, with a siphon tube on the side.
Recognition feature 3 is the raised eyes with horizontal slit pupils and eyelid bumps, built from Ball eyes with a flat RBox pupil, a catch-light and a skin lump over each eye.
Plan, part 1 → shot 1 (wide reef): the bright orange octopus sits on pale sand in front of a mottled grey-brown rock while kelp sways, light shafts drift and a small school of fish passes.
Plan, part 2 → shot 2 (octopus, medium): at t≈0.25 a rock-coloured coat grows over the mantle, head, web and arms, then dark and pale spots and small spikes appear one after another between t 0.28 and 0.40.
Plan, part 3 → shot 3 (eye, extreme close-up): between t 0.42 and 0.54, horn-like skin spikes and bumps grow over the eye, showing the texture change.
Plan, part 4 → shot 4 (reef wide, other angle): between t 0.58 and 0.80 a big blue grouper swims across behind the rock and does not notice the camouflaged octopus.
Plan, part 5 → shot 5 (skin, close-up): seven pigment sacs on the forehead (brown, red, yellow), each ringed by thin muscle strips, widen, shrink and widen again between t 0.82 and 0.98 as the narration says 'cromatóforos'.
The colour change is shown by slightly larger rock-coloured copies of each body part that scale up over the orange ones, so no arrow is needed; the chromatophores sit just outside that coat so they stay visible.
The background rock behind the octopus uses the same camouflage colours and spots, so in the wide shots the octopus visibly blends into it.
The setting is a sand-over-soil-over-rock `Slab` with sand ripples and pebbles under a deep-to-pale blue sea gradient, which contrasts with the pale sand.
There are about 39 environment elements: kelp, sea fans, branching corals, anemones, rocks, starfish and shells; tall ones stand behind the hero and only low ones are in front, so the camera lines stay clear.
Everything stays in the teal-sea colour family, with coral orange as the one warm accent that turns to rock brown.
The eye, skin and fish each have their own named group at the octopus's coordinates, so each gets a full-frame shot by itself.
Ambient motion uses only `Move loop` and sway (siphon and reef bubbles, light shafts, kelp, anemone tentacles, small fish), and the octopus itself never bobs or wobbles.
The octopus is about 3.5 tall with an arm span of about 7 against rocks up to 2.5, so it reads as a large octopus in a real-scale reef.

Accuracy: (1) a soft rounded mantle tilted back behind the head is carried by the Lathe mantle in 'head'; (2) eight curling arms with pale suckers underneath are carried by the 8 Tubes with sucker Balls in 'octopus'; (3) golden eyes with a horizontal slit pupil under a skin brow are carried by Eye (golden eyeball, iris disc, dark slit bar, highlight, brow bulge).
Plan: part 1 'Los pulpos' (t 0-.2) → shot 1 wide 'reef' → the orange octopus sits on the sand in front of the grey rock, bubbles rise from its siphon and a school of small fish drifts past.
Part 2 'pueden cambiar instantáneamente' (t .2-.4) → shot 2 medium 'octopus' → red, brown and yellow chromatophore spots across the mantle, head and arms swell and pulse.
Part 3 'el color y la textura de su piel' (t .4-.6) → shot 3 'head' → at t .44 the skin turns the grey of the rock, rock-coloured bumps pop out at .46 and spikes rise over the mantle and eyes at .48-.56, with the arms and the rock in the frame.
Part 4 'para confundirse con el entorno' (t .6-.8) → shot 4 high-angle 'octopus' → the big blue fish swims past behind the hidden octopus while one front arm stays partly orange to show it is the same animal.
Part 5 'cromatóforos' (t .8-1) → shot 5 'skin' → on a magnified pale patch of the front arm, 12 pigment cells grow from dots to fill their rings and then pulse.
Shot 1 fix: the octopus is now 2x bigger (14 units across, the most the scene can hold), the seabed is its own 44x44 'seabed' block and the wide shot frames only 'reef', so the sand fills the bottom of the frame and the empty sky under it is gone.
Shot 2 fix: the copied rock moved back to z=-10 and the octopus moved forward to z=2, so the head and all eight arms are clear, and the scatter avoid zones keep scenery out of the octopus area and the front camera path.
Shot 3 fix: the mantle, head and eyes are now their own 'head' group, so the camera frames the whole head with the front arms below and the rock behind instead of an extreme close-up of one eye.
Shot 4 fix: the shot now frames the bigger octopus from a high angle instead of the whole reef, and arm 0 is left out of the grey cover after its base, so its middle and tip stay orange as the contrast.
Shot 5 fix: the chromatophores now sit on a magnified patch of the actual front arm (cell ring, pigment disc, dark centre), and the pale strips and spikes that were around the old head patch are gone.
The colour change moved from t .25 to .44 so the octopus is still orange with visible spots in shot 2 and changes on screen in shot 3, matching the narration.
The eyes changed from pale cream to golden with an orange iris disc so the face no longer reads as a pale mask.
Kelp, sea fans, corals, anemones, rocks, starfish, shells, light shafts, bubble columns and the fish school were spread over the larger 44-unit seabed behind and beside the octopus, keeping more than 20 environment elements.

problems: Shot 1: the octopus is tiny and centred on a small floating diorama, so it barely fills the frame. Zoom the camera in or make the octopus about 3x bigger, and widen the seabed block so the empty blue sky below it goes away.

Shot 2: the octopus mantle is cut off by the left rock and the gray patch on the face reads as a mask, not chromatophores. Move the octopus clear of the rock so the whole head and all eight arms show, and add visible coloured chromatophore spots across the skin.

Shot 3: the extreme close-up of the gray spiky head with a pale face and blank dark eyes looks like a mushroom or a rock monster, not an octopus. Pull the camera back so the mantle, eyes and some arms show against the rock it is copying.

Shot 4: the camouflaged gray octopus is small and lost against the gray rock. Make it bigger and move the camera closer, and leave a little contrast (an outline or one arm still partly orange) so the viewer sees it is the same octopus changing colour.

Shot 5: the chromatophore cluster (red, brown and yellow rings) floats on a gray blob with spikes and no skin context, and pale balls are piled around it. Show it as a magnified patch on the octopus skin (an inset or a zoom from the arm), and remove the stray spheres and cones.
